anomalies.observed: Both the ATtiny45 (U1) and ATtiny13 (U4) are powered and have corresponding reset and GPIO pins connected to the same six nets. For example, U1.6 and U4.6 share NET0001, and U1.7 and U4.7 share NET0008.
anomalies.expected: A fan controller should use one active MCU, or provide an explicit means to select between alternative MCUs. Two active MCUs should not have their corresponding GPIOs tied together.
anomalies.impact: If both MCUs are assembled, their outputs can contend on shared GPIO nets, and both may respond to the shared ISP programming signals. This can cause incorrect operation or prevent reliable programming.

parsed.summary: The netlist connects two powered ATtiny devices to the same reset and GPIO nets, with no selection mechanism shown. This creates a likely MCU-to-MCU contention and programming conflict in a design described as an ATtiny-driven fan controller.
